newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-GARCIA KEEPS HIS COOL IN THE HEAT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GARCIA KEEPS HIS COOL IN THE HEAT.

text.p: Mexican Daniel Garcia of Mexico has long been considered one of the world's most talented walkers.
But despite titles at the 1993 World Cup and the 1995 world student games, Garcia's technique under pressure has always been suspect.

He was disqualified at the last two world championships, bitter blows at the time, but on Saturday all the problems of the past paled into insignificance when he won gold in the 20 kms walk on the opening day of the world championships.
"I've been working very hard for this since Atlanta," Garcia said. "I was disappointed with my results there but I went home to Mexico and looked at my technique and training.
"My silver medal at the World Cup in April told me that I had got things right and I've felt for a long time I could win here."
In recent months his bid for victory has involved training on the beach, pounding out the kilometres at the remote location of Ixtapa-Zituatanejo.
On Saturday, Garcia held the lead throught the latter stages of the race after the early leader Russia's Ilya Markov was disqualified with five kilometres to go.
"His disqualification did not matter. I was always sure I was going to catch him in the final kilometres," Garcia said.
Nevertheless, he was pressed hard to the finish by Markov's compatriot Mikail Schennikov.
Schennikov gave up the chase just over a kilometre from the line.
"Daniel got away from me on the last uphill stretch before the stadium and that was the last chance I had," Schennikov said.
Garcia's time of one hour 21 minutes 43 seconds was relatively slow, mainly due to the intense heat. Schennikov was second in 1:21:53 with Belarus's Mikail Khmelnitsky third in 1:22:01.
